# Session 5: Agentic AI

Turn one idea into a tested change: align with an agent, delegate implementation,
then review the result before merging.

## Play the example

This finished game is a demo; your exercise starts from an empty project.

## Set up once

You need Git, Node.js LTS, a GitHub account, and a plan that gives you access
to one coding agent. Choose your agent in the tabs; Codex is the walkthrough.
Start with an empty folder named `tic-tac-toe` and open it in that agent.

::: {.callout-note title="Install the skills and authenticate GitHub"}
Run the installer, select `setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `grill-with-docs`, and
`implement`, and choose your coding agent. Then authenticate GitHub:

```bash
npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills
gh auth login
```

Open the project folder in your agent and run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` once.
Choose GitHub when asked where issues live. See [Matt Pocock's install guide](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills#installation-30-second-setup).

After the starter is committed in step 1, create a private repository (or change
`--private` to `--public` if you prefer):

```bash
gh repo create tic-tac-toe --private --source=. --remote=origin --push
```
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Codex (recommended)

Install and sign in to the [Codex app](https://developers.openai.com/codex/quickstart),
then open the empty project folder. For terminal, follow the [CLI quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/codex/quickstart);
for VS Code, install the [IDE extension](https://developers.openai.com/codex/ide).
Codex supports delegated subagents; request a faster, lower-cost model for the
bounded implementation when available.

## Claude Code

Install [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/getting-started)
or its [VS Code extension](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/ide-integrations).
Open the empty project, authenticate GitHub above, and confirm the extension
supports skills and delegated agents for this exercise. A lighter subagent
model may need a custom agent definition.

## Google Antigravity

Install the [Antigravity VS Code extension](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/extensions/vscode/)
and open the empty project. Confirm that the skills installer offers Antigravity and
that subagents are available. The `flash` subagent model is documented for
Antigravity 2.0 and CLI; support in the VS Code extension is unconfirmed.

:::

## The five steps

### 1. Scaffold, but don't build the game yet

Create and open an empty `tic-tac-toe` folder. Ask your agent for a plain
HTML/CSS/JavaScript project with a README, Node's built-in test runner, a local
server command, and testable stubs. Include a `package.json` with a `test`
script that runs `node --test`; this uses Node's built-in runner without adding
a test-framework dependency. Review and commit this baseline, create the GitHub
repository with the command in the setup card, then make a contribution branch.
The starter must not contain the finished game.

### 2. Agree on the issue and tests

Run `/grill-with-docs` to settle the game rules, boundaries, and checks. Have the
agent write tests first, confirm they fail because behavior is missing, then
publish the agreed specification as a GitHub issue. Include turn order, invalid
and occupied moves, all winning lines, draw, final-move win, terminal state, and
restart. Create an ADR only if a consequential design choice needs recording.

### 3. Delegate implementation

Run `/implement` on the agreed issue. Ask it to use one bounded, lower-cost
subagent if available, preserve the tests, and stop if the implementation scope
needs to change.

::: {.callout-note title="Worker brief"}
Implement the agreed issue on this branch. Keep game rules in one module shared
by the UI and tests. Change only the game and required documentation; do not
weaken tests. Run the checks and report changed files. Stop if the issue and
tests conflict.
:::

### 4. Check the result

Run `npm test`, start the local server using the README command, and play the
game. Confirm X starts; turns alternate; invalid moves do nothing; wins, draw,
and restart work; and keyboard focus and status messages are accessible.

### 5. Review and merge

Ask the agent for a pull request that includes `Closes #<issue-number>` and the
test results. Inspect the diff and try the game yourself. Authorize the merge
only after review, then confirm the issue is closed.

::: {.callout-warning title="You approve the change"}
Read the diff and test results before approving a merge. The agent can propose
and prepare the change; you decide whether it is ready.
:::

## Done when

- [ ] The issue describes the agreed behavior and checks.
- [ ] Tests failed against the stubs, then pass after implementation.
- [ ] The game works in the browser, including win, draw, and restart.
- [ ] You reviewed the pull request and authorized merge.
- [ ] The linked issue is closed.
